home.title: Rodrigo López
home.intro: I design and build systems across the boundary between software and hardware — from embedded firmware and electronics to robotics, full-stack applications, Linux infrastructure, and aerospace engineering. This portfolio documents projects that move from requirements and architecture through implementation, testing, and physical validation.
home.projects_intro: From Bluetooth-controlled robots and microcontroller firmware to full-stack infrastructure and aerospace systems — each one built the same way: define the problem, understand the interfaces, build a testable architecture, integrate hardware and software, validate the result.
home.certifications_intro: Formal training in networking, network security, and engineering, alongside recognition from the international space community.
home.closing_body: I'm interested in engineering and software work involving embedded systems, robotics, electronics, automation, aerospace, telecommunications, full-stack development, and technical R&D. If you're building a system that combines software with real-world hardware, data, or engineering constraints, I'd like to hear about it.

about.title: About Me
body: I'm a Mechatronics and Electronic Engineering student at Universidad del Valle de Guatemala, with experience spanning embedded systems, software development, aerospace R&D, robotics, electronics, digital fabrication, networking, and engineering research.

That work has taken me from university laboratories in Guatemala to aerospace organizations in Boulder, Colorado, and international space-industry programmes. I've developed embedded firmware, integrated sensors and communication interfaces, designed electronic and mechanical systems, supported flight-related biomedical hardware, worked on CubeSat and de-orbit concepts, automated engineering workflows, maintained Linux environments, and built full-stack software infrastructure.

I approach engineering as a systems problem rather than a collection of isolated disciplines. A useful product usually demands the mechanical structure, electronics, firmware, communications, software architecture, manufacturing constraints, testing process, and user requirements be understood at the same time. That multidisciplinary view is the common thread across everything here.
